title: Presence Over Position
goal: Shift focus from seeking positions of power to embracing the power of presence with God and others.
scripture_instructions: Read Mark 9:33-37 in pairs for reflection. Then read Mark 9:42-48 as a group, focusing on its implications for personal growth.

icebreakers.label: A
icebreakers.question: What's a surprising fact about your name or family history?
icebreakers.note: A conversation starter for group bonding.

icebreakers.label: B
icebreakers.question: Think of a time you felt truly served by someone else. How did it impact you?
icebreakers.note: Connects personally with the act of serving.

icebreakers.label: C
icebreakers.question: Share a moment when you wished for more power or recognition.
icebreakers.note: Encourages vulnerability in sharing personal ambition.

sections.title: Serve Without an Agenda
sections.setup: Jesus emphasized serving others without seeking personal gain. He used a child, who can't repay, as the perfect illustration. Serving should be without expectation of return.
sections.say: Let's talk about what it means to serve without looking for return or recognition.

questions.ask: When was the last time you gave or served without expecting anything in return?
questions.lead: Jesus highlighted serving with no expectation of return.
questions.probe: What did you feel at that moment, and was it different from serving with an agenda?

questions.ask: Recall a time you chose to seek another's success over your own. How did it change you?
questions.lead: Being positioned last embraces countercultural service.
questions.probe: What did this reveal about your motives?

questions.ask: Identify an area in your life where you resist being last. How can you change this?
questions.lead: The call to embrace serving others.
questions.probe: How does fear of losing position feed into this?

questions.ask: How can you transform personal ambition into godly ambition in everyday life?
questions.probe: What is one ambition you can redirect this week?

reflection_questions: When have I served without expecting anything in return?
How have I chosen others' successes over my own?
What area in my life resists being last?
How can I transform personal ambition into godly ambition?

sections.title: Surrender Territorial Impulses
sections.setup: Jesus spoke against being territorial, highlighting unity over division. He wants us to work in harmony, even across differences, without competing or claiming exclusive rights.
sections.say: Now we'll consider the challenge of letting go of our need to control and dominate spaces.

questions.ask: When have you felt threatened by someone crossing into your territory at work or home?
questions.probe: What did you do with those feelings?

questions.ask: Think of a time when cooperation yielded better results than competition. How did it alter your approach?
questions.probe: What was your biggest learning from that experience?

questions.ask: How do you typically respond to someone with a different approach or belief system?
questions.probe: Where does this response need to change?

questions.ask: Reflect on a past incident where you guarded your group's 'insider' status. What motivated this?
questions.probe: What would Jesus say to you about this boundary?

reflection_questions: When have I felt threatened by territorial encroachment?
How have I benefited from choosing cooperation?
How do I respond to those with different beliefs?
What motivates me to guard my group's insider status?

sections.title: Stop Tolerating Sin
sections.setup: Jesus uses stark imagery to convey the urgent need to deal with sin radically. He warns against complacency and emphasizes the severe consequences of unchecked sin, urging us towards purity.
sections.say: Let's dig into the weighty matter of sin and how Jesus calls us to cut it off at the root.

questions.ask: What sin or bad habit have you been managing instead of removing?
questions.lead: Radical action against sin is necessary.
questions.probe: How does this management affect your spiritual life?

questions.ask: Can you remember a slip into sin that seemed minor but escalated?
questions.lead: Sin always introduces itself as harmless.
questions.probe: What changes might prevent a repeat?

questions.ask: Identify something in your life that might be a spiritual threat. How will you address it?
questions.lead: Sin's lurking danger beneath the surface.
questions.probe: What first step can you take this week to address it?

questions.ask: Reflect on an area where you've compromised morality. How will you repent and redirect now?
questions.lead: The metaphor of cutting off sin highlights its seriousness.
questions.probe: What's the smallest step towards repentance you can make in the next few days?

reflection_questions: What sin have I been managing instead of removing?
When have I slipped into seemingly minor sin, and what was the outcome?
What might be a spiritual threat I'm ignoring?
Where have I compromised morality and how will I redirect?

closing_go_around: Think of one way you'll prioritize presence over position this week. Let's go around and share our intentions.
prayer: Pray for courage to serve selflessly and for the strength to overcome personal sin. Ask for open hearts towards community and unity.

cheat_sheet.response: Affirm their achievements and reflect on your unique contributions.
Pause and pray for humility and collaboration.
Confide in a trusted friend for support and accountability.
Spend three minutes in silence, inviting God's presence.
Recall a recent moment of God's faithfulness in your life.

key_themes: Serving without seeking gain leads to true greatness.
God calls us to unity and collaboration, not division.
Unchecked sin poses a severe threat to spiritual health.
Jesus wants us to remove sin radically.
Presence with God holds more weight than worldly position.
commitment_prompt: Prioritize one small act of service this week, and ask your accountability partner to follow up.
thesis: Jesus showed that true greatness comes from serving without seeking power, and embracing challenges as part of personal formation.
outline: Surrender the impulse to be territorial
sensitivities: Discussing personal sin may be sensitive; emphasize grace.
Position changes may be raw for those in career transitions.
Encourage reflection not competition on personal achievements.
obstacle: Get honest about the comfort in routine over the discomfort of change initiated by faith.
carry: Next week, ask someone how they noticed God's presence through their service.
